title: Reduce EMR HBase upgrade downtime with the EMR read-replica prewarm feature
key_points: A new EMR feature prewarms a read-replica HBase cluster on S3 so upgrades, AMI refreshes and instance changes become a blue-green switch instead of a long outage.
Three phases (prepare, cut over, validate) with rollback steps.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache HBase, Amazon S3
authors: Suthan Phillips, Ramesh Kandasamy, Mehul Gulati, Rajesh Dhandhukia

title: Build a trusted foundation for data and AI using Alation and Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: A connector syncs catalog metadata between Alation and SageMaker Unified Studio so business and technical teams share the same definitions.
Mostly connector setup: authentication, project access and extraction settings.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Alation
authors: Alation — Anthony Lempelius, James Mesney, Divij Bhatia, Leonardo Gomez

title: Streamline your Amazon Redshift maintenance event notifications with Amazon Simple Notification Service
key_points: Provisioned clusters let the reader move, defer or pick a track (current or trailing) for maintenance; Serverless instead patches in idle time and forces it within a fixed period.
Redshift event subscriptions send maintenance and other cluster events to SNS, set up in the console or with a CloudFormation stack.
RSS feeds track new Redshift versions.
services: Amazon Redshift, Amazon SNS, AWS CloudFormation
decision: Current vs trailing maintenance track, and SNS event subscriptions vs manual checks, for planning around warehouse maintenance
authors: Sushmita Barthakur, Nidhi Nayak, Rajesh Pentapati

title: Modernize game intelligence with generative AI on Amazon Redshift
key_points: Bedrock Knowledge Bases can use Redshift as a structured source: a plain-language question becomes SQL, runs on Redshift and comes back as an answer or summary.
Accuracy depends on context: table and column descriptions, curated example queries, and query history, for example teaching that a country is stored as a code.
Demo on game player telemetry.
services: Amazon Redshift, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Amazon Bedrock
decision: Bedrock Knowledge Base text-to-SQL vs MCP-connected agent vs semantic layer for natural-language questions on warehouse data
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (Redshift Serverless); aws-bytes: GenAI on data (later)
authors: Narendra Gupta, Satesh Sonti

title: How Tipico democratized data transformations using Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow and AWS Batch
key_points: Tipico's central data team offers one Airflow platform where analytics and data science teams run their own container jobs on Batch against the Redshift warehouse.
Shared operators and standard interfaces cut duplicated tooling; Airflow only orchestrates while Batch does the heavy work, which also splits cost per team.
Covers governance and how adoption spread across teams.
services: Amazon MWAA, AWS Batch, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue
decision: Team-owned tooling vs a central orchestration platform with shared operators and container compute for self-service ELT
authors: Tipico — Jake J. Dalli, David Greenshtein, Hugo Mineiro

title: Secure Apache Spark writes to Amazon S3 on Amazon EMR with dynamic AWS KMS encryption
key_points: When one Spark job writes several outputs that each need their own KMS key, EMRFS and S3A cache their settings and can silently encrypt files with the wrong key.
Three fixes compared: turn off the file system cache, use separate Spark sessions or applications, or rely on bucket default encryption.
Advises verifying each object's key afterwards and measuring the performance and S3 API cost of the cache-off option.
services: Amazon EMR, AWS KMS, Amazon S3, Apache Spark
decision: Disable FS cache vs separate Spark sessions vs bucket default encryption for per-dataset KMS keys in one Spark job
authors: Pinxi Tai

title: Get started faster with one-click onboarding, serverless notebooks, and AI agents in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Recap of the late-2025 Unified Studio launches: one-click onboarding with existing IAM permissions, serverless notebooks mixing SQL, Python and Spark, and the built-in Data Agent.
Short customer mentions; little technical depth.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Data Agent
authors: Siddharth Gupta, Matt David, Sean Ma

title: Create a customizable cross-company log lake, Part II: Build and add Amazon Bedrock
key_points: Builds a compliance log lake from CloudTrail and CloudWatch: raw JSON tables for writing, Glue jobs that compact many tiny files into read-optimised ORC tables, and Lambda that adds partitions on arrival.
Glue jobs work on bounded day windows so backfills are routine; AWS reports ORC with ZLIB gave the fastest queries and about half the size of Parquet with Snappy on their log data.
Adds Bedrock model invocation logs and an agent that queries the lake to review another agent's behaviour.
services: AWS Glue, Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon Athena, AWS CloudTrail, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Bedrock
decision: Query raw small JSON files vs separate raw and compacted read-ready tables (ORC vs Parquet) for high-volume logs
authors: Colin Carson, Sean O’Sullivan

title: Top 10 best practices for Amazon EMR Serverless
key_points: Reuse applications as templates, prefer Graviton, start with default worker sizes and only right-size from observed CPU and memory pressure.
Cap scaling with T-shirt-sized limits, pick the right shuffle storage, and use VPC and multi-AZ defaults.
Covers dependency packaging, enforced limits and monitoring via CloudWatch, Prometheus and Grafana.
services: Amazon EMR Serverless, Apache Spark, Amazon CloudWatch
decision: Default workers vs right-sized workers and capped scaling for Spark on EMR Serverless
authors: Karthik Prabhakar, Amber Runnels, Neil Mukerje, Parul Saxena

title: Enable strategic data quality management with AWS Glue DQDL labels
key_points: Glue Data Quality rules can now carry labels such as criticality, owner team, domain or regulation, so failures can be sliced by who must act and how urgently.
Results land in S3 at row and rule level and are queried with Athena grouped by label.
Suggests label naming conventions and routing: page on critical compliance failures, batch the rest into a daily report.
services: AWS Glue, AWS Glue Data Quality, Amazon Athena
decision: Flat rule lists vs labelled rules with owner/criticality routing for data quality alerts across teams
authors: Arun A K, Annie Wang, Roshin Babu

title: Apache Spark 4.0.1 preview now available on Amazon EMR Serverless
key_points: Preview of Spark 4.0.1 on EMR Serverless: ANSI SQL mode, SQL scripting and pipe syntax, VARIANT for JSON, Iceberg v3 and streaming improvements.
Superseded by the later general-availability release, so the preview limits no longer matter.
services: Amazon EMR Serverless, Apache Spark
authors: Al MS, Emilie Faracci, Karthik Prabhakar

title: Access a VPC-hosted Amazon OpenSearch Service domain with SAML authentication using AWS Client VPN
key_points: Reaches a VPC-only OpenSearch domain without a bastion by combining Client VPN, Transit Gateway and SAML sign-in through IAM Identity Center.
Compares the network options for private access before the setup steps.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, AWS Client VPN, AWS Transit Gateway, AWS IAM Identity Center
authors: Jan Michael Go Tan, Kevin Low

title: Power up your analytics with Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio integration with Tableau, Power BI, and more
key_points: Desktop BI and SQL tools (Tableau, Power BI, DBeaver, SQL Workbench) can now reach subscribed Unified Studio data through the Athena JDBC driver while project governance still applies.
Step-by-step client setup for each tool.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon Athena
authors: Narendra Gupta, Durga Mishra, Nishchai JM, Ramesh H Singh

title: On-demand and scheduled scaling of Amazon MSK Express based clusters
key_points: Express brokers rebalance partitions automatically, which makes adding and removing brokers routine instead of a risky manual job.
Two CDK samples: scale on CloudWatch throughput metrics, or scale on a schedule for known peaks.
AWS reports Express clusters give 3x the throughput and 20x faster scaling of standard provisioned clusters.
services: Amazon MSK, MSK Express brokers, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CDK
decision: Fixed capacity vs metric-driven vs scheduled broker scaling for Kafka with daily or seasonal peaks
authors: Subham Rakshit, Rakshith Rao

title: Modernize your data warehouse by migrating Oracle Database to Amazon Redshift with Oracle GoldenGate
key_points: Moves an Oracle warehouse to Redshift in four steps: DMS Schema Conversion for objects, GoldenGate for the initial load, GoldenGate CDC with its Redshift handler, then cutover.
Continuous replication keeps the source live until switch-over, which keeps downtime short.
Mostly setup detail (networking, secrets, GoldenGate on EC2).
services: Amazon Redshift, AWS DMS Schema Conversion, Oracle GoldenGate, Amazon EC2
decision: DMS full load + CDC vs Oracle GoldenGate for moving an Oracle warehouse into Redshift with minimal downtime
authors: Sachin Murkar, Ravi Teja Bellamkonda, Bipin Nair

title: Managing Amazon OpenSearch UI infrastructure as code with AWS CDK
key_points: Deploys the new OpenSearch UI with CDK and uses a Lambda to create workspaces and dashboards through the saved-objects APIs, so dashboards are versioned like code.
Adds VPC access and fine-grained access control settings.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, AWS CDK, AWS Lambda
authors: Zhongnan Su, Paul-Andre Bisson

title: Accelerate context-aware data analysis and ML workflows with Amazon SageMaker Data Agent
key_points: Deep dive on SageMaker Data Agent in Unified Studio notebooks: it reads catalog metadata and notebook state to plan and write SQL, Python and Spark for a multi-step analysis.
Demo analyses NYC taxi trips through to a simple ML model; covers guardrails and data privacy.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Data Agent, AWS Glue Data Catalog
authors: Kshitija Dound, Siddharth Gupta, Ishneet Kaur, Mohan Gandhi, Murali Balakrishnan Narayanaswamy, Shubham Mehta, Amit Sinha, Vikramank Singh

title: Streamline large binary object migrations: A Kafka-based solution for Oracle to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon S3
key_points: Splits an Oracle migration in two: Debezium on MSK Connect streams row changes into Aurora PostgreSQL, while Lambda pulls each large object and stores it in S3 with a link back to its row.
Avoids LOB size limits and truncation, and suits migrations that run in parallel with the source for a long time.
CDK code on GitHub; covers limits and operational practices.
services: Amazon MSK, Amazon MSK Connect, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, AWS Lambda, Amazon S3, Debezium
decision: Migrate LOBs inside the database vs stream rows and offload LOBs to S3 for long-running Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migrations
authors: Naresh Dhiman, Archana Sharma, Ron Kolwitz, Karan Lakhwani

title: How Bazaarvoice modernized their Apache Kafka infrastructure with Amazon MSK
key_points: Bazaarvoice moved from self-run Kafka to MSK to stop spending engineering time on patching, upgrades and scaling.
Covers planning, migration problems they hit, and a staged consumer cutover so no messages were lost or double-processed.
Lists lessons learned for teams doing the same move.
services: Amazon MSK, Apache Kafka
decision: Keep self-managed Kafka vs move to MSK, and how to cut consumers over safely
authors: Bazaarvoice — Oleh Khoruzhenko, Aravind Marthineni, Christian Silva

title: Enterprise scale in-place migration to Apache Iceberg: Implementation guide
key_points: Converts existing Parquet tables to Iceberg without rewriting files, using either migrate plus register_table or add_files, run as Glue or EMR Spark jobs.
A DynamoDB control table tracks each table's migration state so large batches are repeatable and restartable.
Warns about table ownership: dropping a managed Iceberg table deletes the data, so protect source files during cutover.
services: Apache Iceberg, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Amazon DynamoDB, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Athena
decision: migrate/register_table vs add_files vs full rewrite for moving Parquet/Hive tables to Iceberg
authors: Mihir Borkar, Arghya Banerjee, Amit Maindola

title: Using Amazon EMR DeltaStreamer to stream data to multiple Apache Hudi tables
key_points: One Hudi MultiTable DeltaStreamer job on EMR reads several MSK topics and upserts each into its own Hudi table, with a shared config plus per-table overrides.
Runs CDC-style incremental syncs on a fixed interval and registers tables in the Glue catalog for Athena.
Useful mainly as a contrast to Iceberg-based streaming paths, which AWS increasingly favours.
services: Amazon EMR, Amazon MSK, Apache Hudi, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Athena
decision: One multi-table Hudi streamer vs a job per table vs an Iceberg streaming path for many Kafka CDC topics
authors: Gautam Bhaghavatula, Sucharitha Boinapally, Veera Bhargav Nunna, Radhakant Sahu

title: Unlock granular resource control with queue-based QMR in Amazon Redshift Serverless
key_points: Redshift Serverless now supports query queues inside one workgroup, each with its own monitoring rules, instead of one rule set for every query.
Queries are routed by user role or query group, so ETL, BI and ad hoc work get separate limits and runaway queries can be logged or aborted per queue.
Includes advice on identifying workload types and sizing queue thresholds.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift Serverless
decision: Workgroup-wide rules vs per-queue rules vs separate workgroups for isolating ETL, BI and ad hoc load on Redshift Serverless
authors: Srini Ponnada, Davide Pagano, Ashish Agrawal, Niranjan Kulkarni

title: How Slack achieved operational excellence for Spark on Amazon EMR using generative AI
key_points: Slack built a Spark listener that streams job, stage and task metrics to Kafka and lands them in Iceberg, giving a per-job history of runtime, memory, skew and spill.
An analytics MCP server exposes that history to coding assistants, which use Bedrock-hosted models and a fixed prompt to suggest concrete Spark settings.
AWS reports Slack cut Spark costs by 30-50% and job runtimes by 40-60%.
services: Amazon EMR, Amazon Bedrock, Apache Spark, Apache Kafka, Apache Iceberg, Apache Airflow
decision: Expert hand-tuning vs metrics-history-driven AI recommendations for Spark job configuration
attaches_to: aws-bytes: GenAI on data / cost optimization (later)
authors: Slack — Avijit Goswami, Nilanjana Mukherjee, Tayven Taylor, Mimi Wang, Rahul Gidwani, Prateek Kakirwar

title: Access Snowflake Horizon Catalog data using catalog federation in the AWS Glue Data Catalog
key_points: Same federation pattern as the Databricks post, this time pointing the Glue Data Catalog at Snowflake Horizon Catalog over the Iceberg REST endpoint.
Snowflake-side steps (roles, access token, catalog-linked database) are the bulk of the work; Lake Formation then controls who sees what in AWS.
Queried from Athena with no data duplicated between the platforms.
services: AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon Athena, Apache Iceberg, Snowflake Horizon Catalog
decision: Scheduled copy from Snowflake vs catalog federation over Iceberg for cross-platform analytics
authors: Snowflake — Andries Engelbrecht, Nidhi Gupta, Pratik Das, Srividya Parthasarathy

title: Navigating architectural choices for a lakehouse using Amazon SageMaker
key_points: Frames lake-centric and warehouse-centric lakehouses as complementary and explains how one catalog layer and Iceberg REST access let many engines share the data.
Compares four storage choices: plain S3 files, self-managed Iceberg on S3, S3 Tables, and Redshift managed storage, with when each fits.
Also covers ingestion options into the lakehouse and how permissions attach at the catalog.
services: Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Apache Iceberg, Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Redshift, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lake Formation
decision: Plain S3 files vs self-managed Iceberg vs S3 Tables vs Redshift managed storage for each layer of a lakehouse
authors: Lakshmi Nair, Saman Irfan

title: Access Databricks Unity Catalog data using catalog federation in the AWS Glue Data Catalog
key_points: The Glue Data Catalog can federate to Databricks Unity Catalog over the Iceberg REST API, so Iceberg and UniForm tables there show up in AWS without copying data or syncing metadata.
Lake Formation still applies fine-grained permissions on the federated tables; access is read-only.
Setup covers Unity Catalog external access, a secret and IAM role, the federated catalog, and querying from Athena.
services: AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon Athena, Apache Iceberg, Databricks Unity Catalog
decision: Copy or sync tables from another platform vs read-only catalog federation over shared Iceberg tables
authors: Srividya Parthasarathy, Venkatavaradhan Viswanathan

title: Use Amazon SageMaker custom tags for project resource governance and cost tracking
key_points: SageMaker Unified Studio project profiles can push required or default tags onto every resource a project creates, to satisfy SCP tag rules and cost reports.
API and CLI only in the first release; shows profile setup and checking that resources got the tags.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon DataZone
authors: David Victoria, Ahan Malli, Rohit Srikanta

title: Create AWS Glue Data Catalog views using cross-account definer roles
key_points: Catalog views can now be created with a definer role that lives in a different account from the base tables, which is what data mesh setups with a central catalog need.
The view shares a filtered subset of columns and rows while base tables stay private; one view carries both a Spark and an Athena dialect.
Walkthrough spans a central and a producer account using Lake Formation sharing.
services: AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR
decision: Share base tables vs share filtered multi-dialect catalog views (cross-account definer) in a multi-account data mesh
authors: Aarthi Srinivasan, Sundeep Kumar

title: AWS analytics at re:Invent 2025: Unifying Data, AI, and governance at scale
key_points: Roundup of the re:Invent 2025 analytics launches: SageMaker one-click onboarding, serverless notebooks and Data Agent, Iceberg improvements, governance features, and OpenSearch for AI.
Also lists cost and performance items such as self-managing materialized views and serverless storage for EMR.
Useful as a checklist of what changed, not as a guide to any one feature.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon Redshift, AWS Glue, Amazon EMR, Apache Iceberg, AWS Lake Formation, Amazon OpenSearch Service
decision: Which late-2025 launches change the default lakehouse and warehouse design choices
authors: Larry Weber

title: Building scalable AWS Lake Formation governed data lakes with dbt and Amazon Managed Workflows for Apache Airflow
key_points: A metadata file drives everything: Airflow DAGs are generated from dbt tags, and Lake Formation tags and grants are created from the same metadata instead of by hand.
dbt with the Athena adapter moves data raw to formatted to published zones, with a custom audit table and a step that quarantines records failing quality checks.
Ends with practical advice on running dbt inside MWAA workers (resource exhaustion, dependency clashes, large DAG counts).
services: Amazon MWAA, AWS Lake Formation, dbt, Amazon Athena, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon S3
decision: Hand-written DAGs and grants vs metadata-generated DAGs and Lake Formation tags for a governed dbt-on-Athena lake
authors: Abhilasha Agarwal, Muralidhar Reddy

title: Amazon EMR Serverless eliminates local storage provisioning, reducing data processing costs by up to 20%
key_points: EMR Serverless can now hold Spark shuffle data in managed storage, so jobs no longer need local disks sized up front and no longer fail when a skewed partition fills a disk.

Because shuffle is no longer pinned to workers, idle executors are released between stages; AWS reports up to 20% lower processing cost overall and up to 80% less compute in funnel-shaped benchmark queries.
Opt-in per application or per job, with guidance on when to keep local disks.
services: Amazon EMR, Amazon EMR Serverless, Apache Spark
decision: Sized local shuffle disks vs managed serverless shuffle storage for Spark jobs with skew or uneven stages
authors: Karthik Prabhakar, Matt Tolton, Neil Mukerje, Ravi Kumar Singh

title: Simplify multi-warehouse data governance with Amazon Redshift federated permissions
key_points: Warehouse namespaces are registered in the Glue Data Catalog and auto-mounted everywhere, so a grant, row-level policy or masking rule written once follows the data to whichever warehouse runs the query.
Identities come from IAM or IAM Identity Center instead of local users created per warehouse.
Walkthrough applies RLS and dynamic masking on one warehouse and shows a read-only user on a second warehouse seeing only the permitted slice.
services: Amazon Redshift, AWS Glue Data Catalog, AWS IAM Identity Center
decision: Per-warehouse local grants vs federated permissions stored with the data for a multi-warehouse Redshift estate
authors: Satesh Sonti, Ning Di, Sandeep Adwankar, Ramchandra Anil Kulkarni, Abhishek Rai Sharma
